title: One of Several Kinds: A Command That Can Only Be What It Says, and a Compiler That Checks You Handled Them All

questions.question: A command struct has a kind number and a field for everything any kind needs. What can it hold that makes no sense?
options: A stop with wheel speeds left in it, a drive whose speeds were never set, and a kind that is none of the three
questions.explanation: Nothing says which fields belong to which kind.

questions.question: What does a default-constructed std::variant<Stop, Drive, SetLimit> hold?
options: The first alternative, Stop, which is why Stop must be constructible without arguments

questions.question: The command holds a Drive. What do get_if<SetLimit>(&c) and get<SetLimit>(c) do?
options: get_if gives nullptr and get throws std::bad_variant_access
questions.explanation: One is a polite question and one is asking as if sure.

questions.question: A fourth kind is added to the variant and the visitor is not changed. What happens?
options: It does not compile: there is no function for the new kind
The new kind is ignored with a warning
questions.explanation: The lesson's checks/ snippet is expected to fail to compile, and it does.

questions.question: Driving at 0.8 and -0.4 and then setting a limit of 0.5, what are the wheel speeds?
options: 0.5 and -0.4: the limit clamps what is happening now, not only the next drive
questions.explanation: A drive of 3 and -3 afterwards gave 0.5 and -0.5.

questions.question: What is sizeof a variant, compared with its alternatives?
options: The sum of all of them
The largest alternative plus a tag: 24 against Drive's 16 on the machine measured
questions.explanation: The three added up came to 25.
